QF.id: Concept and Role of Mutual Fund_24

question.text: An AMC wants to launch a new equity scheme called "Growth Opportunities Fund" that will invest in high-growth mid-cap and small-cap companies. Under SEBI categorization norms, the AMC can launch this scheme ONLY if:

answer.text: It does not already have a scheme in the same SEBI-defined sub-category, as only one scheme per sub-category is generally permitted
It merges all existing equity schemes into this single new scheme first
It obtains approval from RBI since this involves equity market participation
The scheme name includes the SEBI category name verbatim in its title

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook (page 53), SEBI categorization permits an AMC to have only one scheme per category, with specified exceptions for index funds/ETFs, Fund of Funds, and sectoral/thematic funds. Page 48 records the SEBI 2017 categorization objective of standardising and distinguishing schemes, and page 78 supports the resulting consolidation toward one scheme per category. The Trap: Option B is extreme — only schemes that did not fit the new categorization had to be merged, re-categorized, or wound up. Option C is wrong because SEBI (not RBI) regulates mutual funds. Option D is incorrect because the scheme name does not need to repeat the SEBI category name verbatim. Note: The one-scheme-per-category rule, with its narrow exceptions (index/ETF, FoF, sectoral/thematic), is the operative SEBI constraint on new scheme launches in this scenario.
